data.narrative:
Fortem Technologies is a Series C-stage defense and security company that has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 10 peers spanning both public equities (2 companies: DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and private ventures (8 companies), with particular focus on three same-sector, same-stage private comparables: Castelion ($13.0B), Stark Defence ($4.0B), and Neros ($2.5B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. The stage-progression method, anchoring to the $100M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yields $170M. The peer-median approach leverages the three defense and security Series C comparables, which exhibit a median valuation of $4.0B against a range of $2.5B to $13.0B. This wide dispersion reflects material differences in scale and market positioning within the peer set.

Synthesizing both methods produces an implied valuation range of $144M (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The substantial gap between the stage-progression result and peer-median reflects uncertainty around Fortem's competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized peers. Resolution of this spread depends on relative progress in revenue generation, customer concentration, and technology differentiation versus the peer cohort.
